newsitem.title: USA: UAL still on track for better Q2 - Greenwald.
newsitem.headline: UAL still on track for better Q2 - Greenwald.

text.p: UAL Corp was still on track to beat its second quarter performance of a year ago, chairman and chief executive officer Gerald Greenwald said Wednesday.
Greenwald played down the effect on United Airlines of the grounding of Great Lakes Aviation Ltd, an Iowa-based company that operates some commuter flights as United Express.
"We don't see an impact," Greenwald told reporters after addressing UAL's annual meeting here, explaining that Great Lakes was the smallest of its regional operators.
Great Lakes said Tuesday that it might not be able to resume flying Thursday as it had earlier hoped.
Asked whether UAL Corp, the parent of United Airlines, was still on track to better its year ago performance in the second quarter, Greenwald said simply "yes."
UAL earned $2.52 per fully distributed share in the second quarter of 1996.
"Business is good, profits are better," Greenwald told reporters in summing up recent performance.
UAL last month reported first quarter earnings of $1.61 per share on a fully distributed basis, up from $0.72 a year ago before a debt extinguishment charge.
Greenwald told shareholders that United Airlines was back where it belonged, "at the head of the industry."
He said the annual meeting coincided with an effort to widen that lead.
The airline had spent two years conducting research, which found that airline customers were deeply dissatisfied with the industry in general and saw United as just another big airline.
Starting Thursday, United would launch its new advertising campaign that stressed empathy with travelers and highlighted what the airline was doing to meet their expectations.
One spot showed at the meeting featured footage of early attempts to fly, combined with an audio track that included flight cancellation announcements.
United is shelving its familiar "friendly skies" slogan during the campaign in favor of a United Airlines "rising" logo.
